articles.title: Could the Universe Be Just Right for Life Because of How Liquids Flow?
articles.summary: Scientists found that if the universe's basic rules changed even a tiny bit, water and blood could become as thick as tar. That would make life impossible. A new study says the same rules that shape stars also control how liquids move inside living cells.

articles.title: May's Moonless Nights Are Your Best Chance to See the Milky Way's Glowing Heart
articles.summary: In mid-May, the moon disappears, making the sky extra dark. That's the perfect time to spot the Milky Way's bright core arching across the southern sky. You'll need to get away from city lights and look between midnight and dawn. It's like a glowing ribbon made of countless stars.

articles.title: A Pond Creature Just Rewrote the Rules of DNA
articles.summary: Scientists found a tiny organism in a pond that reads DNA instructions in a totally new way. It changed the meaning of two 'stop' signals, which usually tell cells when to end a gene. This breaks a rule scientists thought was almost universal in all living things.
